title: One-click manual Reject on a queue card: no confirmation, silent candidate email, no undo
expected: Rejecting a candidate from an AI review card — an irreversible, candidate-facing action — asks for confirmation (or previews the rendered rejection message), confirms the send afterward, and offers a way back.
got: AiReviewCard's Reject is a single click; the card animates out optimistically and the API unconditionally dispatches the rejection email (route.ts:262) with no confirmation of the send. The reconsider/undo queue joins only `auto_rejected` events, so a manually rejected candidate never appears in it (documented as deliberate).
suggested_acceptance: A queue-card Reject shows a confirm step naming the candidate and the message that will be sent; after the send, an explicit confirmation states what went to whom; a mis-clicked manual reject has a recall/reinstate path (or the reconsider queue includes recent human rejects).
l2_priority: Reject one candidate from a screening card live: verify the email lands in the Channels outbox with no UI confirmation, and that the candidate is absent from the reconsider queue.
scope_note: Sending mechanics are comms-scope; this finding is about the decision affordance (confirm/undo/feedback), which is Decisions-scope.

title: Null match score coerces to 0 — an unscored candidate is auto-rejectable on a fabricated number
expected: A candidate with no match score (never scored / degraded intake) is excluded from the auto-reject wave or flagged 'unscored' for manual review; a sealed adverse record never asserts a measurement that was not taken.
got: runScreenWave sorts and thresholds on `matchScore ?? 0` with no null exclusion in the cohort filter — a never-scored candidate ranks worst, passes `0 < maxMatchToReject`, and (unless fairness-protected by archetype) is auto-rejected with a sealed rationale claiming 'match 0 < 45'. The preview shows them as 'match 0', indistinguishable from a genuine zero, so the human gate cannot reliably catch it.
suggested_acceptance: An entry with matchScore=null at Screened is either excluded from the wave cohort (listed separately as 'unscored — needs review') or visibly marked unscored in the preview; a sealed record never renders a null score as 0.
l2_priority: Seed a Screened entry with matchScore=null (e.g. degraded intake), open the wave: confirm whether it appears as 'match 0' in the would-reject list and what the sealed record says after commit.

title: Auto-rejection email has no automated-decision disclosure and no contest / human-review channel
expected: A candidate adversely affected by automated processing is told automation was involved and offered a route to request human intervention / contest the decision (GDPR Art. 22(3), AI Act transparency).
got: dispatchRejection sends the same template for auto and manual rejects; the copy reads 'After careful review, we won't be moving forward' — implying individual human review of an automated threshold decision — with no automation disclosure and no contest affordance. The GDPR footer covers data access/erasure only. The reconsider path exists but is recruiter-initiated and invisible to the subject.
suggested_acceptance: The rejection comm for an auto-rejected candidate (dispatchRejection with automated:true) includes a plain-language sentence disclosing automated processing with human approval, plus a reply/link channel to request human re-review; the manual-reject template stays as-is.
l2_priority: Commit a small wave and read the actual outbox message body for an auto-rejected candidate — confirm the absence of disclosure/contest language in both locales.
scope_note: Comms delivery/channels are out of journey scope; this is the content of the decision notice, judged under Lucie's disclosure lens.

title: Sealed record of a human decision omits the AI recommendation it ratified
expected: When a recruiter accepts/rejects from an AI screening card, the sealed decision record captures what the AI recommended (verdict, confidence, rationale, model/source) so a right-to-explanation dossier shows both the machine input and the human call.
got: The human accept/reject seal writes only { fromStage, detail } as inputs with a default rationale like 'Recruiter accept from Screened'. The AI recommendation lives in mutable approval_detail (set by automation-run) and is cleared on decision — the chain cannot reproduce what the human saw. Model/version is captured nowhere in the record.
suggested_acceptance: For an accept/reject on an entry carrying a *_review approval, the sealed inputs include the approval payload snapshot (recommendation, confidence, source) and the payload's model/source field; the dossier for that candidate shows the AI input alongside the human decision.
l2_priority: Accept one AI screening card live, then export the decision dossier for that candidate and confirm the AI recommendation is absent from the sealed record.

title: approvedBy in the immutable record is unauthenticated free text, defaulting to a generic constant
expected: The 'who approved this reviewed set' claim in a sealed Art. 22 record names an authenticated person.
got: The route accepts any `approvedBy` string from the request body with no identity check; absent one, operatorApprover() writes 'operator (single-operator deployment)' (or KP_OPERATOR_NAME if set). The code documents this seam honestly — but the central attribution claim is either generic or client-suppliable.
ceiling: Single-operator deployment with no per-user identity: a truly authenticated approver name requires the multi-user auth layer; until then KP_OPERATOR_NAME is a deployment precondition, and the client-supplied approvedBy should be dropped or bound to the session.
suggested_acceptance: The commit path derives approvedBy from the server-side session/env only (never the request body); deployments without KP_OPERATOR_NAME get a startup/UI warning on the records panel.
l2_priority: Commit a wave, export the dossier: confirm what approvedBy actually reads in the sealed record on this deployment.

title: Role row shows pending-decision chips but the wave acts on the whole Screened cohort — counts differ, scope unexplained
expected: The wave modal states whose cohort it operates on, and the discrepancy with the row that launched it (N chips vs M cohort) is self-explanatory.
got: RoleDecisionRow renders entries with approvalKind='decision' (the pending queue slice); runScreenWave's cohort is ALL active entries at stage 'Screened' for the jobId. The modal shows the server cohort count but never explains the scope, so the recruiter may believe the wave targets the chips they just saw.
suggested_acceptance: The wave modal's subtitle names the cohort ('all N candidates at Screened for this role'), so a count differing from the row is explained before the preview renders.
l2_priority: With a role whose pending-chip count differs from its Screened cohort, open the wave and check whether the mismatch is noticeable/confusing live.

title: Reinstate restores the pipeline but offers no candidate follow-up, though the rejection email already went out
expected: Reinstating an auto-rejected candidate prompts (or at least reminds about) a follow-up message — the candidate was already told 'no' under the bank's name.
got: reinstatePipelineEntry restores active@Screened and seals the reversal, but deliberately sends nothing ('re-notifying them is a deliberate recruiter follow-up, not auto-sent here'), and the Reconsider UI offers no follow-up affordance or reminder — the correction is invisible to the candidate unless the coordinator remembers.
ceiling: Auto-sending a 'we are re-reviewing' note is deliberately avoided (a reinstate may be exploratory); the gap is the missing *affordance/nudge*, not the missing auto-send.
suggested_acceptance: After Reinstate, the row (or a banner) reminds that a rejection note was already delivered and offers a one-click localized follow-up draft.
l2_priority: Reinstate a rejected candidate live: confirm they return active@Screened and observe what, if anything, points at the already-sent rejection.

title: Per-candidate decision dossier (?candidate=) has no UI consumer — DSAR response is export-all-and-filter
expected: A candidate-scoped 'view/export this subject's sealed decision record' affordance (from the records panel, reconsider row, or candidate drawer) for right-to-explanation / DSAR responses.
got: The API supports ?candidate=<entryId> scoping (documented as the right-to-explanation dossier) but the only consumer, DecisionRecordsPanel, fetches unscoped; no Decisions/Reconsider affordance links a candidate to their sealed records. Flagged by two prior harness passes; still unwired at 3395b4c.
suggested_acceptance: From the records panel (or the candidate drawer), one click scopes to a single candidateRef and exports that subject's dossier; the chain verdict stays global with copy noting integrity is chain-wide.
l2_priority: Confirm live that no navigation path yields a candidate-scoped records view.

title: AI screening card rationale/strengths/red-flags render in English inside the Czech workspace
expected: The screening recommendation a Czech coordinator ratifies reads in Czech, like the wave's DEC4-localized rationales do.
got: automation-run passes --lang only for the 'prep' task; the screen task's LLM output (rationale, strengths, redFlags in approvalDetail) is English and AiReviewCard renders it verbatim, while all surrounding chrome is Czech.
suggested_acceptance: The screen task receives the workspace locale (mirroring prep) or the card renders a structured localized mirror, so the ratification surface is fully Czech.
l2_priority: Open a live screening_review card with LOCALE=cs and confirm the mixed-language render.

title: Ship-bar: /api/decisions/* routes carry no in-route auth or tenant scoping; the decision chain is workspace-less
expected: On the public product path, screen-wave commits, sealed records, and the reconsider queue are session-authenticated and scoped to a workspace/tenant.
got: screen-wave, records and reconsider handlers perform no auth/tenant check in-route, and decision_records has no workspace column — one global chain. Acceptable in the current single-operator dev-gate deployment; a cross-tenant leak (and unauthenticated adverse-action commit) on the multi-workspace path env.md describes.
suggested_acceptance: Decisions routes require a valid session on the production path and every decision record carries + filters by workspace id.
l2_priority: Probe GET /api/decisions/records and POST /api/decisions/screen-wave without the dev gate / session and record what answers.
scope_note: Ship-bar capture (public product path) — near-zero live impact in the current single-operator deployment; ranks below the every-run findings.

title: Strength: preview-first wave with a server-enforced human-approval token (Art. 22 gate is structural, not copy)
got: Dry-run on open + every slider change with zero mutation; commit requires the SHA-256 approval token of the exact previewed reject set, recomputed server-side from the live cohort; missing/stale token → 409 → forced re-preview; the commit loop reads from the same signed set so committed ≠ reviewed is impossible.
suggested_acceptance: Protect: do not weaken the token gate for convenience (e.g. auto-retry commit after 409).

title: Strength: fairness gate is server-side and fail-closed; tie-break never splits equal scores, resolved in the candidate's favour
got: Early-career AND unknown/renamed archetypes are shielded from auto-rejection at the decision point (not just in UI copy); unknown archetypes write a drift marker on commit; the tie-safe cutoff keeps a straddling tied run whole (kept, not rejected); small cohorts get a documented min-1 policy so an enabled rule can't silently no-op.
suggested_acceptance: Protect: keep the gate at the decision point; never move shielding into client-side filtering.

title: Strength: tamper-evident decision chain covering the auto-reject, the human decision, AND the reversal, with verify + one-click export
got: Auto-rejects seal policyVersion + approver + decisive inputs; reinstatements seal the reversal (an overturned rejection is not an audit hole); human accept/reject seals too; verifyDecisionChain recomputes every link and the Analytics panel headlines the verdict and exports the chain with a localized rationale alongside the byte-stable sealed English.
ceiling: Records are best-effort (sealDecisionSafe never throws) — a seal failure logs and proceeds, so the chain is near-complete, not guaranteed-complete; and human-decision records are thin (SD-L1-004).

title: Strength: screening override validated + clamped at the route AND re-validated at the destructive operation
got: A malformed/out-of-range override is a 400 at the boundary, and runScreenWave re-validates before merging into the live config — a raw {rejectBottomPercent:9999} can never reach the bottom-% math through any caller; only clamped known fields merge.

title: Strength: reconsider queue makes the auto-reject undo real — guarded, audited, and sealed
got: Auto-rejected candidates surface in a collapsed always-available queue with match score + rejection date; Reinstate is CAS-guarded to still-rejected entries (double-click/stale view is a 409, not churn), restores active@Screened, records a reinstated event, and seals the reversal into the chain.
ceiling: Undo restores pipeline state only — the already-sent rejection email is not recalled and no follow-up is prompted (SD-L1-007).

title: Strength: localized rationales render from a structured mirror while the sealed English string stays byte-stable
got: reasonCode/reasonParams mirror the audit rationale so a Czech recruiter/auditor reads Czech (would/did phrasing picked from the run's dryRun flag; tie-adjustment noted) while the hashed record never changes; cs.json carries the full decisions.wave/reasons/rules/compliance catalog (verified).

title: Strength: commit shows its deltas at the moment of irreversibility — stale skips and per-candidate comms failures are named, not counted
got: A candidate whose stage changed mid-wave becomes a visible 'skipped' keep-row (no phantom audit event, no email); a rejection whose notification failed to queue is badged per-row ('needs a manual nudge') in the committed view, backed by a rejection_comms_failed event — the wave never half-fails silently.
